unresolved: Bolnick full text was inaccessible through the attempted primary endpoint. The 40.4% variance comparison is not independently verified and is omitted from accepted findings; even a valid AMOVA comparison would not prove language descent.
No universal 8,000–10,000-year ceiling for comparative linguistics is accepted from this synopsis; dating and recoverability depend on evidence and methods.
No chapter-level count of families versus isolates was checked. “Around 50 families and numerous isolates” risks conflating categories and is not used.
Brown’s supplied DOI remains unresolved independently; the publisher title, authors, year and scope were verified through its book page.

Greenhill’s abstract age range is a model estimate; its reference year and full calibration assumptions were not checked, so no calendar conversion or closed language-distribution interval is assigned.
corrections: Na-Dené and proposed Dene–Yeniseian relationship are not equivalent levels of classification. The PDF’s “linked by consensus” and “confirm” wording is replaced by attributed model language.
Urban and Guzmán Naranjo investigate a continental structural gradient; that result is not a demonstration of Dene–Yeniseian descent or an observed migration.
Greenhill’s northern Uto-Aztecan origin is one model, not a disproof of every southern or agricultural scenario. Preserve the existing Nakatsuka alternative and distinguish genes from language.
Greenhill pages are 81–107, not RIS 107–181 or PDF 107–81. Institutional DOI is 10.1353/lan.2023.0006; supplied 10.1353/lan.0.0276 remains in provenance.
10.2307/417069 identifies Doris Bartholomew’s 1999 review of Campbell’s 1997 book, not a Campbell-authored 1999 original study.
Thomason’s handbook review belongs to Language 82(4), December 2006, not 2007.
Kilarski and Silver–Miller are books, although the RIS labels them JOUR; Brown author initials are expanded from publisher metadata.
Brown’s book proposes Aleut–Utian and challenges familiar affiliations; its publisher description cannot be recast as general consensus support for the synopsis family table.
Ward’s historical use of Amerind and placement of Haida in Na-Dene are not adopted. Sicoli–Holton explicitly treat Haida as an unrelated isolate outgroup.
Typological traits, genetic correlations, language family membership and community identities are separate evidence categories. No family is assigned to ancient genomic samples.
